macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks finish mixed as Fed minutes signal further tightening
items.summary: The Dow fell 1.1% to 50,198.17, the S&P 500 declined 0.2% to 7,323.63, and the Nasdaq gained 0.4% to 24,429.88. Federal Reserve minutes showed officials broadly supporting additional rate increases to contain inflation, with some open to a hike larger than 25 basis points if inflation data worsen.[10]

items.title: Nvidia beats earnings expectations but shares decline
items.summary: Nvidia reported quarterly results above analyst expectations and forecast revenue above estimates, supported by strong data-center demand. Its shares nevertheless fell about 2.9% as investors focused on leadership uncertainty, regulatory risks and broader technology-sector weakness.[9][10]

items.title: Fed officials deliver additional hawkish signals
items.summary: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said the central bank needs to respond more aggressively to persistent inflation, while Governor Michael Barr said further rate increases would be appropriate if economic conditions follow his current outlook.[5][9]

items.title: ECB reportedly considers doubling bank reserve requirements
items.summary: European Central Bank policymakers are reportedly preparing to discuss raising the eurozone minimum reserve ratio for commercial banks from 1% to 2%. The discussion could take place on November 25 or be deferred to December 17.[5]

items.title: U.S. industrial output falls in October
items.summary: U.S. industrial production declined 0.4% in October after rising 0.7% in September, adding to evidence of weaker momentum in the manufacturing sector.[4]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $64,000 as crypto liquidations approach $2 billion
items.summary: Bitcoin traded near $63,874, down 1.69% over 24 hours and 13.48% over seven days, while Ether fell 1.89% to about $1,790. Roughly $2 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated, including approximately $774 million in Bitcoin contracts and $488 million in Ether contracts.

items.title: World Bank explores stablecoin payments with Circle and Citi
items.summary: The World Bank has begun an exploratory initiative with Circle and Citigroup to assess whether stablecoins can improve cross-border payments and make development-finance transfers more traceable. No payment service or transaction volumes have been announced.

items.title: Backpack receives U.S. futures commission merchant approval
items.summary: The National Futures Association approved Backpack to operate as a futures commission merchant, following earlier U.S. approvals for its derivatives-market and clearing operations. The exchange says the authorization will support leveraged perpetuals and event contracts for U.S. customers.

items.title: Germany considers 180-day Bitcoin freeze powers
items.summary: A Bundestag-backed proposal would reportedly allow German authorities to freeze Bitcoin held through custodial exchanges for up to 180 days. The proposal would not require self-custody users to surrender private keys.

items.title: NEAR approves 1.6% token-emission cap
items.summary: NEAR governance approved proposal HSP-029, setting a maximum token emission of 1.6% over 24 months.

items.title: Stacks launches vote on Bitcoin deposits and Clarity 7
items.summary: Stacks opened a governance vote covering its 4.1 upgrade, including proposed changes related to Clarity 7 and Bitcoin deposits.

items.title: Lighter withdrawals reportedly halted after suspected $15.5 million breach
items.summary: Lighter reportedly paused crypto withdrawals and new liquidity-pool creation after suspected unauthorized activity drained approximately $15.5 million from two market-maker accounts.

items.title: ICE considers operating a Solana validator
items.summary: Intercontinental Exchange is considering running a Solana validator, according to ICE Clear Europe president Hester Serafini at Solana Breakpoint in London.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Microsoft announces Decision-1.1 and enterprise AI updates
items.summary: Microsoft made Decision-1.1 generally available, a lower-cost model for software decision-making, and announced the rollout of its long-running productivity agent, Autopilot, through its Frontier program.

items.title: NVIDIA introduces Nemotron for scientific discovery
items.summary: NVIDIA announced Nemotron for Science, including an open dataset and post-training recipes designed to adapt Nemotron models for agentic work in life sciences and chemistry.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly launched GPT-6.2 Astra for complex professional work and GPT-6.2 Sol for more efficient everyday tasks. The report also describes lower pricing and expanded availability across OpenAI products.

items.title: Shanghai AI Laboratory releases Sage S2.1-Flash
items.summary: Shanghai AI Laboratory reportedly released Sage S2.1-Flash under the MIT license, a 321-billion-parameter scientific multimodal model designed to process molecular graphs, crystal structures, and protein data.

items.title: NVIDIA releases open Nemotron Sigma model
items.summary: NVIDIA reportedly published Nemotron-Labs-Sigma-8B, an open 8-billion-parameter continuous-diffusion language model on Hugging Face.

items.title: Tencent Hunyuan open-sources Hy4 Flash
items.summary: Tencent Hunyuan announced the open-source release of Hy4 Flash, including standard, FP8, and base variants distributed through major model repositories and developer platforms.

items.title: Reson8 open-sources multilingual speech model
items.summary: Reson8 reportedly released Rumble-2-Flash under the Apache 2.0 license. The 0.5-billion-parameter speech-recognition model supports more than 40 languages and automatic language detection.

items.title: NVIDIA unveils GR00T 2 robotics model
items.summary: NVIDIA reportedly unveiled GR00T 2, an open robotics world-action model intended to predict how robot actions change visual observations, alongside updates to its robotics simulation tools.

items.title: Study reports language models can predict protein sequences
items.summary: A reported study found that Anthropic’s Claude models predicted amino acids in little-studied proteins better than shuffled-sequence baselines, suggesting potential applications in biological research.

items.title: Microsoft expands specialized enterprise AI models
items.summary: Microsoft expanded its proprietary AI portfolio at Ignite with specialized models targeting coding, cybersecurity, image generation, speech, transcription, and decision-making.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches amid record anticipation
items.summary: Rockstar’s Grand Theft Auto VI is rolling out worldwide for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S after a 13-year wait. The launch has driven strong interest in consoles, with UK retailer John Lewis reporting a 62% year-over-year increase in gaming-console and accessory sales over the past three weeks.

items.title: Take-Two shares rise ahead of GTA VI release
items.summary: Take-Two Interactive rallied before GTA VI’s launch as reported preorders surged and early reviews were highly positive. The game is launching on current-generation PlayStation and Xbox consoles, while PC and Nintendo Switch 2 versions have not been announced for launch.

items.title: Firaxis reportedly cuts about one-third of workforce
items.summary: Firaxis Games, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, reportedly eliminated approximately 60 jobs, representing about one-third of its staff. The layoffs are among the latest significant workforce reductions in the game industry.

items.title: Nintendo releases Splatoon Raiders demo for Switch 2
items.summary: Nintendo released a free demo for Splatoon Raiders, a Switch 2 exclusive, giving players an early opportunity to try the upcoming title.

items.title: Esports commentators criticize AI-generated The Finals coverage
items.summary: Esports casters criticized Embark Studios after the developer replaced human talent in a highlight reel for The Finals’ Grand Major Qualifier with the game’s AI commentators, prompting calls for changes to how esports broadcasts use AI.

items.title: Kingen re-signs with Nongshim RedForce
items.summary: League of Legends player Hwang “Kingen” Seong-hoon has re-signed with Nongshim RedForce, according to Inven Global’s esports coverage.
